_: The personalization grammar of spec/frame-v2.md section 11, as data. Both strings of a pair are checked and not one, because the server's encoder takes the client's decoder string. Every case here is a rule that was found missing or found wrong rather than a rule that was already held: the randomness floor was measured on the whole string, which let one random character pass behind a long host, and the byte cap was measured in UTF-16 code units on the browser side. Transports are the three names wire.Transport prints. The Go side drives conn.PersonalizationPrefix and conn.ValidPersonalization from spec/conformance; the TypeScript side drives src/protocol/personalization.ts. Regenerate with gen_personalization.py.

grammar._: randomness_min counts characters of the randomness SEGMENT, which ends at the first slash after the prefix. max_bytes counts UTF-8 bytes of the whole string, never UTF-16 code units.

_pad: A case carrying a pad appends char, count times, to value before anything is measured. It is there so a 1024 byte fixture is one readable line rather than one unreadable one.
_errors: prefix: the string does not begin with this transport's prefix. randomness: the randomness segment is under the floor. too_large: over the byte cap. control: a byte under 0x20, or 0x7f, anywhere in the string. A case names the first failure and not every failure, so the order of the checks is pinned as well as the checks themselves.
_known_gap: The grammar writes randomness as 22 or more characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Neither implementation checks the alphabet, and both measure the floor in bytes, so 11 two byte characters clear it. The two agree, so no pair fails over it, and the cases above pin the behaviour that exists rather than the one the grammar describes. Closing it means an alphabet check landing in conn/pairing.go and in personalization.ts in the same change, because a floor one end enforces and the other does not is a pair that cannot be made.

minted._: A generator must produce a string its own validator accepts for the transport it was minted for and refuses on the other two. That is the property the prefix exists for and the one a generator can get wrong without any single case above catching it. Only the TypeScript side drives this: the Go generator is unexported in conn and the exported surface is the validator alone.
